name: tcn
label: TCN (stock, reference)
what_it_assumes: the last ~60 cycles, read through fixed sliding filters, show how close the cutter is to breaking

name: linear_hazard
label: Logistic hazard (linear)
what_it_assumes: risk is a fixed weighted sum of today's readings; the past doesn't matter

name: mlp_now
label: MLP on today only
what_it_assumes: risk is any smooth function of today's readings; the past adds nothing once today is known

name: gru
label: GRU
what_it_assumes: a 64-number running summary, updated every cycle, can carry everything about the past that matters

name: lstm
label: LSTM
what_it_assumes: like the GRU, plus a separate memory cell that can hold early-life facts for a long time

name: transformer
label: Causal transformer
what_it_assumes: any earlier cycle may matter, and the network learns which ones to look back at

name: tcn_direct
label: TCN, direct regression
what_it_assumes: same window as the TCN, but the answer is a single number of cycles left, not a risk curve

name: tcn_currents_only
label: TCN, motor currents only
what_it_assumes: the motors' electricity alone carries the wear signal

name: tcn_vibration_only
label: TCN, vibration only
what_it_assumes: the accelerometers alone carry the wear signal

name: tcn_summaries
label: TCN on the 120 summaries
inputs: 120 released summaries + settings + age (126; LightGBM's inputs)
what_it_assumes: the dataset's own per-cycle summaries carry the wear signal as well as our physics features

name: tcn_no_age
label: TCN without age
inputs: physics features + settings + first_ring, no log_age (28)
what_it_assumes: wear shows in the signals themselves, so the cycle count is not needed

name: tcn_age_only
label: TCN on age only
what_it_assumes: all cutters age alike, so the cycle count alone says how much life is left
